item.title: Missouri sits on one of America’s most active earthquake zones
item.description: When most people think of earthquakes, they think of California fault lines. But the most active earthquake zone east of the Rocky Mountains runs straight through the middle of the country — including parts of Missouri.

item.title: Florissant City council approve $5M be used for roads, facility parking lots
item.description: Potholes and deteriorating roads across Florissant have frustrated residents for years, but a new proposal introduced and approved Monday night could soon bring relief.

item.title: Legislation can limit how fast certain drivers can go
item.description: This house bill would require drivers whose licenses have been revoked for consistent reckless driving to enroll in the Intelligent Speed Assistance Program if they receive a court order.

item.title: Lawmakers debate gifted student screening bill
item.description: Lawmakers in the Missouri House are expected to approve a new round of legislation this week, including a measure that would require school districts to expand existing efforts to screen all students for gifted programs.

item.title: 6 homes near Coldwater Creek to be demolished
item.description: Demolition is underway in north St. Louis County, where six homes are being torn down for radioactive contamination linked to Coldwater Creek.

item.title: St. Louis woman dances into her 101st birthday
item.description: Surrounded by family, friends, and familiar faces, Lela McSpadden marked a milestone few ever reach: her 101st birthday.

item.title: Homeowner blames St. Louis Water Division after tree falls on house
item.description: A tree fell on a Baden home in north St. Louis, narrowing missing two people inside. The homeowner says it is the fault of the city Water Division.

item.title: Festus residents push back against potential data center
item.description: The council recently approved a rezoning request that could open the doors for a developer to present a plan.

item.title: Ex-police chief gets $200K payout amid misconduct claims
item.description: $200,000 to walk away. That’s what Ballwin’s former police chief, Douglas Schaeffler, was paid out in a settlement finalized at the end of 2025. The settlement includes a deal that allows Schaeffler to obtain his full benefits through his government retirement system

item.title: ‘It could have been any one of us’: Police wife raises funds for SLMPD officers injured by fleeing vehicle
item.description: It will be a long journey of healing for two St. Louis police officers badly injured in the line of duty. And their friends are calling on the community for support.
